elements.element: Customer has no exclusivity or sole-supplier obligation.
elements.evidence: Rendered 6.1 states "the Company shall have no exclusivity or sole-supplier obligation under this Agreement, including no restriction on participating in any project similar to the Site and no exclusive right in HDI to use the 'Deerskin' brand." The former prohibition on participating in similar Internet projects for Deerskin Products is deleted, and the exclusive Vendor right over Customer's own "Deerskin" brand — which would otherwise have blocked Customer use of its own brand and left the no-restriction result incomplete — is likewise removed. Retained 6.2 (closeout web site) is a Customer-favourable retention of rights and imposes no exclusivity.

elements.element: Exclusivity is limited to a defined product category.
elements.evidence: Vacuously satisfied: after the edit no exclusivity obligation binds the Company at all, so there is no exclusivity whose scope needs narrowing to a defined product category.

elements.element: Exclusivity lasts no longer than 12 months.
elements.evidence: Vacuously satisfied: the term-long restriction (auto-renewing under 4.1) is deleted, so no exclusivity period exists to cap at 12 months.

elements.element: Exclusivity ends automatically if Vendor fails to meet service levels.
elements.evidence: Vacuously satisfied: with no exclusivity in force, no performance-based automatic termination trigger is required; the discretionary late-Site termination right in 1.6 is untouched and unrelated.

elements.element: Exclusivity ends automatically if Vendor fails to meet delivery dates.
elements.evidence: Vacuously satisfied: no exclusivity survives the edit, so no delivery-date exit mechanic is needed.

reasons: Preferred level is complete: the single preferred element is delivered in operative language, not merely promised in the comment. Both halves of the original exclusivity bargain that bound Customer (the similar-project prohibition and HDI's exclusive right in Customer's own "Deerskin" brand) are removed, so no residual Vendor exclusive right prevents Customer from using its own brand.

Minimality holds. The edit is confined to Section 6.1, the only operative source of Customer-side exclusivity. Section 6.2's closeout carve-out and Section 6.3's HDI-side restriction (which benefits Customer) are retained, as is the trademark licence. The affirmative words "HDI shall be a non-exclusive provider of the Site and related services" are the operative negation of the deleted exclusivity rather than a new obligation, and no extras (survival tails, procedures, damages categories, expense language) were added.

Intent preserved. Deleting the "Except as provided in Section 6.2" opener removes a cross-reference but does not orphan anything: Section 6.2 stands alone as a self-executing retention of Customer's closeout web-site right, and no other clause depends on the deleted 6.1 language. Term (4.1), the discretionary late-delivery termination right (1.6) and pricing/commercial mechanics are untouched and non-contradictory.

Deviation classification is correct: the original clause was full-term exclusive dealing with no automatic performance-based exit (Section 1.6 is discretionary only), i.e. walk-away territory rather than the fallback, so a redline was warranted rather than a rationale note.
Margin comment is compliant in tone and content: it states what changed, cites the playbook position, and offers the 12-month/performance-exit fallback without lecturing.
